narrationTexts: I'll start by finding what's still using the old API.
Pattern is uniform. Migrating all 12 in-repo files:
Now verifying — check what's left and that everything still parses:
finalText:
Migration is complete. 12 files, 36 call sites converted from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

All files pass `node --check`. There's no package.json or test suite in the repo, so no tests to run.

**One call site deliberately left alone:** `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13` still calls `db.query`. It's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4 with a header saying it's replaced wholesale on every upgrade and local edits are silently lost — migrating it in place would be reverted by the next vendor bump. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query()` entirely, that's a real blocker worth tracking separately: either upgrade legacy-orm to a version that uses `execute`, or wrap the vendored module behind a local shim that translates positional calls. Let me know if you want me to build that shim.

I also left `cache.query(...)` calls untouched throughout — that's `lib/cache.js`, an unrelated API.
